title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
prompt:
Return `true` if `nums` can be split into two subsets whose sums are equal.

**Example**: `[1,5,11,5]` → `true` (`[1,5,5]` and `[11]`). `[1,2,3,5]` → `false`.

**Constraints**: `1 <= nums.length <= 200`, `1 <= nums[i] <= 100`.
hints: If the two halves are equal, what must each half sum to? Does that make some inputs impossible right away?
The question becomes: can some subset sum to total / 2? Let dp[j] = some subset of the numbers so far sums to j, with dp[0] = true, and add the numbers one at a time.
`for (int j = target; j >= x; j--) dp[j] = dp[j] || dp[j - x];`. Loop j downwards so each number is used at most once.

solution.explanation: A subset summing to total / 2 leaves the rest summing to total / 2 as well, so this is subset-sum (an odd total fails immediately). dp tracks reachable sums as numbers are added. Going through j backwards means dp[j - x] still reflects the state before x, so no number is used twice. O(n · total) time, O(total) space.
